RagShortTexts: After Alamut fell, Syrian assassins at Masyaf used hidden blades to survive among Mamluks.

Variants.Content: With Persian Alamut destroyed, Syrian Nizari Ismailis held fast across Masyaf and Jabal Bahra. Devoted fida'i operatives undergo years of disguise as servants or grooms before striking with poisoned daggers. Both crusader princes and Mamluk emirs pay tribute to avert sudden death in their pavilions.

No commander sleeps without trusted bodyguards at his door. Ever since Conrad of Montferrat was struck down by disguised friars, any delayed courier payment to Masyaf brings nightmares of silent steel.
Never cross quiet travelers sitting alone in wayside inns. A slender dagger tipped with viper venom can slip between coat plates before a man can draw his arming sword.
